_note: Loose family: members share STRUCTURE, the lexicon concept-inventory, and the title-ladder pattern, but each realizes phonology per sub-palette. Mutual intelligibility is moderate (shared civic/feature roots; divergent endings).

phonology.palette: Mediterranean: vowel-rich (a e i o u), liquids l/r, sibilant s, stops p t k b d g, f/v; moderate onset clusters (st tr pr kl sp); generally open syllables.

sub_palette_notes.iberian: Latinate with Celtic substrate; endings -briga/-ica/-o; harder c, occasional -nt-.

phonology.phonotactics: CV / CVC; vowel-final preferred; clusters limited to st/tr/pr/kl/sp; geminates allowed.

lexicon_concepts._note: Concept inventory; cultures realize each per sub-palette in their own kit.lexicon.

shared_roots._note: A few civic/feature roots recognizable family-wide as cognates, giving the moderate mutual intelligibility.

morphology_template.toponymic_suffixes: settlement = [feature | founder | deity] + civic suffix; suffix set per sub-palette (latinate -um/-ia/-polis; hellenic -os/-eia/-polis; iberian -briga/-ica).
morphology_template.patronymic_form: inherited clan/gens name as a binomial or trinomial element; not a prefix-patronymic.
morphology_template.gendered_endings: male/female vowel endings per sub-palette (latinate -us/-a; hellenic -os/-e; iberian -o/-a).
morphology_template.compounding_rule: [adjective|resource](stem) + feature-word, eliding before a vowel; OR feature-word + civic suffix; linking vowel where needed.

title_ladder_structure._note: ACKS domain tiers; ruler and domain titles RHYME (shared stem + ruler-suffix / domain-suffix). Tier -> ruler-level mapping pending the ACKS lookup (gdd-history-simulation §17).
title_ladder_structure.rhyme_rule: ruler = stem + ruler-suffix; domain = stem + domain-suffix (e.g. Rex / Regnum).
title_ladder_structure._government_note: Only feudal and clanhold governments are mechanically modeled; republics/oligarchies/theocracies are narrative flavor only.

conventions.people_name_default: personal + inherited clan + optional earned cognomen/agnomen; order personal-first.
conventions.transparent_vs_opaque: moderate; civic and feature names often transparent, ancient/sacred names opaque.
